Equation reference: eq:nonzero. For \(x\in D\) with \(a(x)>0\), the exact operator identity is \[
 L_0\psi(x)=2\delta a(x)(1-\psi(x))
             \int_{\mathbb R^n}b(y)k_0(x-y)\,dy>0 .\] Take a small ball allowed in Lemma 6.6 meeting this support. The actual choice \(c_0=\mathop{\rlap{\ensuremath{\mkern 3mu-}}\int}\nolimits_{\Omega_R}(v/\psi)\) is positive, so [eq:forcing] (#eq:forcing) is nonzero even for the coefficient selected in the proof, not merely for an irrelevant arbitrary constant. One can arrange \(a(x_0)=b(x_0)=0\) at the freezing point while \(a\) is positive elsewhere in that ball. Then (1.9) freezes \(\widetilde K\) to \(k_0\) exactly, and (6.12) gives back \(\widetilde K\). Thus this obstruction also occurs in the actual locally frozen setup of Lemma 6.7.

Take \(n=2\), \(s=3/4\), \(\sigma=1/4\), \(\varepsilon=1/8\), \(q=\infty\), \(u(x)=x_1\), \(R=1\), \(x_0=0\), and a constant fractional kernel. The affine function is locally in the required energy space and belongs to \(L^1_{2s}\), since its tail integral is proportional to \(\int_1^\infty r^{-2s}\,dr<\infty\). Its principal-value operator is zero by oddness. All hypotheses hold with \(f=0\). The source defines \((u)_{B_\rho}\) as the average of \(|u|\) (page 10). Reflection symmetry and \(|a-m|+|-a-m|\ge 2|a|\) imply, for every \(m\in\mathbb R\), \[\mathop{\rlap{\ensuremath{\mkern 3mu-}}\int}\nolimits_{B_\rho}|x_1-m|\,dx
 \ge \mathop{\rlap{\ensuremath{\mkern 3mu-}}\int}\nolimits_{B_\rho}|x_1|\,dx
 =\frac{4\rho}{3\pi}.\] Taking \(m=(u)_{B_\rho}\), we therefore obtain \[\mathop{\rlap{\ensuremath{\mkern 3mu-}}\int}\nolimits_{B_\rho}|u-(u)_{B_\rho}|\,dx
 \ge \frac{4\rho}{3\pi},
 \qquad \beta=\frac98.\] The right side of the proposed estimate is a fixed finite multiple of \(\rho^{9/8}\), an impossibility as \(\rho\downarrow0\). The proof’s step from a \(C^\beta\) seminorm to a pointwise difference of order \(|x-y|^\beta\) is invalid when \(\beta>1\).
